# Scope and method

- Product as defined in the brief: the Antigravity App, CLI and SDK. Every value rests on a page of antigravity.google, the vendor's Google Cloud documentation, the vendor's public SDK repository, or the installed CLI's own help, all read on 2026-11-12.
- Base URL for the documentation is `https://antigravity.google`. A path such as `/docs/teamwork` means `https://antigravity.google/docs/teamwork`.
- "Availability" repeats what the page says. Where a page carries no label, the cell says "no label on the page" and does not claim general availability.
- Quotes are exact. Line breaks inside a quote are removed.

# The 25 services

| Group | Service | Value | Quote | URL | Availability |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| Runtime | Harness | **yes** | "It provides a secure, stateful runtime harness that handles tool execution, context management, safety policies, and subagent delegation." The App and CLI "run the same agent". | /docs/sdk/overview ; /docs/features | App and CLI: no label on the page, all plans. SDK: "in preview" (/blog/introducing-google-antigravity-sdk). |
| Runtime | Sessions | **yes** | "You can return to a prior conversation at any time to continue an implementation, refine a solution, or recover from an interrupted session." Also: "Remote agent conversations are stored with your remote projects rather than on your machine." | /docs/cli/conversations ; /docs/remote-agents | No label on the page. Resume, fork and rename in the CLI; search and history in the App. |
| Runtime | Tasks | **part** DISPUTABLE (yes) | "Each time the agent attempts to finish, a goal stop hook checks whether the goal is still active. If it is, the agent receives a reminder with the time spent so far, the continuation count, and the original request." | /docs/commands/goal | No label on the page. Reason: `/goal` tracks one objective (goals are listed "with their Active, Completed, or Cancelled status"), keeps the original request and can be canceled; `/tasks` lists background commands, timers and subagents. No per-task retry or recovery is described (searched: retry, recover, resume after). Yes is defensible because the stop hook makes the agent continue until the goal is verified. |
| Runtime | Environments | **yes** | "Antigravity Remote Agents run your agent sessions and tools in an isolated, Google-managed remote environment rather than on your local machine." Also: "New worktree mode: Creates a new Git worktree for the conversation." and "The terminal sandbox isolates agent shell commands inside OS-level container boundaries to protect your workstation and sensitive files." | /docs/remote-agents ; /docs/projects ; /docs/sandbox | Worktrees and sandbox: no label (sandbox is "enabled by default" in the App). Remote Agents: Google AI Pro and Ultra personal accounts only. |
| Runtime | Scheduling | **part** | "Automations (previously called scheduled tasks) let you plan ahead with your projects by sending messages to your agents on a schedule, even while you’re away." | /docs/features ; /docs/commands/schedule ; /docs/sidecars | Automations: App only, no label. Reason: start at a time is supplied (Automations, `/schedule` timers and cron). Start on an event is a mechanism the user builds on (sidecars are "useful for persistent background scripts, scheduled recurring tasks, and reacting to events"; SDK "Triggers"). No limit on how much may run at once was found (searched: concurren, at the same time, maximum, queue). |
| Runtime | Lifecycle | **yes** | "Subagents run asynchronously in the background. At any point during a session, a subagent exists in one of three states." (Running, Idle, Killed.) Also: "manage_subagents: List or terminate active subagents." | /docs/subagents ; /docs/hooks | No label on the page. The list is per conversation (`/agents` panel); Swarm members add Active, Waiting, Killed (Swarm is "in preview"). |
| Knowledge | Memory | **part** | "Agents don’t remember conversations. If you spend twenty minutes teaching the agent that your repository’s tests must run with a particular flag, that knowledge disappears when the conversation ends, unless it’s written down as a customization." | /docs/commands/learn | No label on the page. Reason: `/learn` writes a lesson into a rule or skill after the user approves it; `@conversation:` lets the agent look up a past conversation. No record of where an entry came from and no upkeep of entries is described. "knowledge items" appear only as a name for files in the app data directory (/docs/agent-settings) and in the 2025 launch post; no current page documents them (/docs/knowledge returns 404). |
| Knowledge | Retrieval | **yes** | "The remote agent reads attached Drive files on demand during conversations." Also: "Type @ in the message box to mention files, folders, rules, and past conversations". | /docs/remote-agents ; /docs/features ; /docs/mcp | Mentions and MCP: no label. Drive resources: Remote Agents plans only. |

Loading: "On every turn, the agent sees a list of available skills with their names and descriptions. Swarm's shared board with @mentions: "in preview", Pro and Ultra. Events reach registered hook handlers, mentioned Swarm members and timers; no general publish and subscribe between agents is described. |
| Interaction | Orchestration | **yes** | "Teamwork organizes multi-agent collaboration into clear orchestration, implementation, and verification tiers" and "Project plan artifact: Tracks the milestone roadmap, active workstreams, and dependency flow." | /docs/teamwork | `/teamwork`: "available on paid plans"; named "/teamwork-preview command" and "(Preview)" in the Gemini Enterprise administrator settings. `/swarm`: preview. People take part through the scoping interview, plan approval and permission prompts. |
| Interaction | Channels | **yes** | "Remote Control allows you to drive and monitor your Antigravity App sessions and Antigravity CLI instances across multiple machines from any web browser" and "Run the CLI non-interactively to script agent tasks, integrate with CI pipelines, and capture machine-readable output." | /docs/features ; /docs/cli/headless | No label. Channels found: desktop app, terminal, six IDE extensions (Agent Client Protocol), web and mobile browser with push notifications, voice mode, headless JSON, SDK. No chat, email or messaging-platform channel was found (searched: slack, google chat, gmail, telegram, whatsapp, webhook). |
| Governance | Identity | **part** | "Engineers log in using their existing enterprise identity, giving agents secure, authenticated access without manual API key setup." | /blog/antigravity-enterprise ; /docs/enterprise | Enterprise sign-in (SSO, Workforce Identity Federation, ADC): generally available in the App, CLI, VS Code and Visual Studio; preview in other IDEs. Reason: the person's identity is established and can be signed out. No identity per agent, no record of the person accountable for an agent identity and no revocation of an agent identity were found (searched: revoke, service account, on behalf, identity). |
| Governance | Secrets | **part** DISPUTABLE (yes) | "Your OAuth credentials are encrypted at rest and tokens are securely injected when the remote agent makes requests to authorized services." | /docs/remote-agents | Remote Agents plans only. Reason: the quote covers connected plugins in remote agents; the sandbox also blocks "Sensitive files such as ~/.ssh and .env". Locally, MCP credentials sit in configuration ("Access tokens are stored in ~/.gemini/antigravity/mcp_oauth_tokens.json.", bearer tokens in `mcp_config.json` headers) and no general store that releases a value at the point of use is described. Yes is defensible for remote agents alone. |
| Governance | Policy | **part** DISPUTABLE (yes) | "Precedence rule: Conflicting rules are strictly evaluated in priority order: Deny > Ask > Allow." Enterprise: "Specify a list of allowed URLs that the agent can access in the browser. When configured, the system blocks all other URLs." | /docs/permissions ; https://docs.cloud.google.com/gemini/enterprise/docs/ai-developer-tools-settings | No label. Reason: rules decide whether an action proceeds and grants are issued (`access_grants`, allow rules). Content is governed only by where the agent may read and browse (domain, file and MCP rules). For stored data only logging switches and a user-requested deletion were found, not rules on what is kept. Yes is defensible on the action and grant clauses. |
| Governance | Approvals | **yes** | "access_grants (array of strings): Scoped, pre-approved permissions, such as command(gh issue list), read_file(/abs/path), write_file(/abs/path), mcp(<server>/<tool>), or read_url(github.com)." Single actions: "When the agent encounters an operation requiring approval (Ask mode), an interactive card appears in your editor." | /docs/sidecars ; /docs/permissions | No label. Advance approvals are recorded as allow rules in settings and as `agent_permissions` in an automation's `sidecar.json`. |
| Operations | Observability | **yes** | "The absolute path to the persistent transcript.jsonl conversation logs." Enterprise: "Enable full audit logging with one toggle to capture prompts, agent tool executions, and generated artifacts." | /docs/hooks ; /blog/antigravity-enterprise | Transcripts, sidecar logs, `/agents` detail view, headless `stream-json` events with token usage: no label. Audit logging: Gemini Enterprise, off by default. |
| Operations | Evaluation | **part** | "Auditor: Validates work against the selected integrity mode and checks test evidence against real command output, ensuring tests genuinely passed rather than being mocked or skipped." | /docs/teamwork | Paid plans; preview label in enterprise settings. Reason: work products are checked against agreed criteria (Teamwork Critic, Challenger, Auditor, Success Auditor; Swarm verifier; `/goal` evidence check). No result of "unknown" when a check could not run was found, and no evaluation of agent behavior over many runs (the home page says only that the SDK can "run evaluations on top of the Antigravity agent harness"). |
| Operations | Improvement | **part** DISPUTABLE (yes) | "The /learn command asks the agent to reflect on recent interactions and propose durable changes" | /docs/commands/learn | No label; App, CLI and IDE. Reason: the evidence is the current conversation only and the proposals are rules or skills, not agents or the platform; the user starts it. Yes is defensible because it turns corrections and failed attempts into a reviewed proposal ("learning_proposal.md"). |
| Operations | Releases | **part** | "An Antigravity plugin is a versioned, self-contained bundle defined by a plugin.json manifest." | /blog/plugin-marketplace-in-antigravity ; /docs/plugins | Marketplace launched 2026-10-29. Reason: plugins carry a version and install, update, enable, disable and uninstall as a unit; the CLI updates itself. No way back to an earlier version of a plugin, agent, skill or rule was found (searched: downgrade, pin, previous version, rollback, revert). `/rewind` rolls back conversation history only. |
| Operations | Reliability | **part** DISPUTABLE (yes) | "Antigravity manages the lifecycle of sidecars, automatically launching them and restarting them if they crash or error." | /docs/sidecars ; /docs/remote-control ; /docs/changelog (CLI v1.2.1) | Sidecars: App only. Reason: restart is described for sidecars and for the Remote Control daemon ("Comes back by itself after a crash"), and model API errors "automatically retry in-process with exponential backoff". Restoring an agent's running work after the app or host fails is not described. Yes is defensible for the background services the product itself runs. |

Counts: yes 13, part 12 (5 of them DISPUTABLE toward yes), no 0, not assessed 0.

# Four further questions

## 1. Areas of work (C1 to C4 of rerate-criteria-v2)

| Criterion | Value | Quote and location | Reason |
|---|---|---|---|
| C1 | **part** DISPUTABLE (yes) | "The /teamwork command runs a collaborative multi-agent team designed for large software projects, complex simulations, and deep research tasks." (/docs/teamwork). Other candidate: "A project is a configuration of folders defining the environment and the scope of your agent." (/docs/projects) | The units that hold several agents are a Teamwork team and a Swarm, each built for one task, which rates part. Yes is defensible if a Project counts as an area of work: it is a defined element, several agents work in it ("These settings can be modified and apply to all agents within this project.") and a user has many projects. The pages define a project as folders, settings and permissions, not as an area of work, so the lower value stands. Plugins and Marketplace categories ("Business", "Productivity & Project Management") group capabilities but are packaging units. |
| C2 | **part** DISPUTABLE (yes) | "All projects have their own isolated agent settings, allowing you to customize each project’s security settings independently." (/docs/projects) | A project specifies scope (folders), settings and permissions at the level of the unit, but neither what the unit is responsible for nor roles. Yes is defensible for a Teamwork team: its "Request artifact: Captures your initial prompt, goals, constraints, and testable acceptance criteria." and its roles (Sentinel, Project Orchestrator, Explorers, Workers, Critic, Challenger, Auditor, Success Auditor) are defined apart from the agents that fill them. That unit exists for one task. |
| C3 | **part** | "Its brief, which says what it owns, what it must not touch, and what “done” looks like, is posted to the board so every member can see who is doing what." (/docs/swarm). Also: "the Project Orchestrator assigns specific files to individual Workers." (/docs/teamwork) | The board and the project plan artifact are kept records that name one owner per piece of work or file while a run lasts. They are records of assignments taken on at run time, not a record of one accountable area per responsibility or capability. |
| C4 | **part** DISPUTABLE (yes) | "description \| string \| (Required) \| Detailed description used by the planner to determine when to delegate tasks to this agent." (/docs/subagents, frontmatter table). Also: "Flexible routing: Agents can communicate with parent agents, subagents, or peer agents whose ID is known." | Agents can discover other agents (custom agent definitions with descriptions, `manage_subagents` list, Swarm roster) and reach them (`invoke_subagent`, `send_message`). Matching a kind of work to an agent happens inside the delegating agent's own reasoning over those descriptions; no directory element answers a lookup. Yes is defensible because any agent with subagent tools can use the descriptions to pick and call a handler at run time. |

Directory (derived): C3 part, C4 part, so **part**.

## 2. Supplied agents for an area of work

Supplied by the vendor, each inside software engineering, data or science:

- Built-in subagents, not tied to an area: "research: Optimized for codebase research, file navigation, and structural exploration.", "browser", "self" (/docs/subagents).
- Teamwork roles for software and research projects: "Critic: Performs independent code reviews, evaluating correctness, logical completeness, robustness, interface conformance, and adherence to project code style." (/docs/teamwork).
- Flutter accessibility agent: "Flutter partnered with Antigravity to launch the Flutter Accessibility custom agent." (/blog/custom-agents-in-google-plugins, 2026-09-28).
- Firebase Security Rules agent: "The agent is part of the official Firebase plugin, which you can easily enable right from your settings." (same post).
- Science skills: "Curated collection of agent skills for scientific computing and research workflows." (/docs/build-with-google).
- Data engineering skills: "Specialized suite of skills and MCP tools for data engineers and database practitioners building end-to-end analytics, ETL, and AI workflows on Google Cloud." (/docs/build-with-google).
- Other "Build with Google" bundles are skills for a technology stack (Firebase, Android, Chrome DevTools, Dart and Flutter, Google Maps Platform, Google Cloud, Modern Web Guidance, Antigravity SDK), and the Google Workspace plugins (Calendar, Docs, Drive, Sheets, Slides) are connectors.

Not supplied by the vendor: agents or roles for finance, sales, marketing, operations or other business areas. The use-case pages for those areas tell the user to build them: "Save monthly close checks, FX normalization rules, and cohort retention audits as repeatable Skills your finance team can run." (/use-cases/finance). Marketplace plugins under "Business" (for example Zoho CRM, Stripe, Zapier) come from partners. The first-run question "what best describes your work—Software Engineering, Knowledge Work, Data & Analytics, Science, Design, or Other" sets a layout and starter prompts; "No plugins are installed when you pick a role" (/docs/getting-started).

## 3. What fits nowhere

- Quota, credits and budget control: "Granular budget caps and pooled quotas: Set monthly budget thresholds in Google Cloud Billing across projects, teams, and individuals." (/blog/antigravity-enterprise); `/usage` "to help you monitor your resource consumption" (/docs/cli/commands/usage); the "AI Credit Overages user setting" (/docs/plans).
- Inline code completion in the editor: "Supercomplete provides code suggestions in a region near your current cursor position." (/docs/ide/tab).
- A person's own version-control work in the product: "The Antigravity App provides a Git-native Review pane for the changes in your project." with stage, commit, amend and push (/docs/features).
- Interface layouts chosen by kind of work: "switch between the Knowledge Work layout (focused on conversation, documents, artifacts, and folder outputs) and the Software Engineering layout" (/docs/features). This changes what a person sees, not a platform responsibility.

## 4. Where it runs and what the user supplies

- **Where.** Both. Local by default: the App is "Your command center to manage multiple local agents in parallel." (home page); the CLI and SDK run on the user's machine (the SDK "relies on a compiled runtime binary"). Vendor cloud as an option: "Antigravity Remote Agents run your agent sessions and tools in an isolated, Google-managed remote environment rather than on your local machine." (/docs/remote-agents), limited to "Google AI Pro and Google AI Ultra subscribers who sign in with a personal Google Account"; "It isn’t available on the free plan, on Google AI Plus, or for business accounts".
- **When the user is away.** Remote: "Remote Agents continue working on long-running tasks and executing commands even when you close your browser, put your laptop to sleep, or switch between desktop and mobile devices." Local: the host must stay on. Remote Control "Requires your host machine to remain powered on and online" (/docs/remote-agents table); "If an agent is running, Antigravity prevents your computer from sleeping." (/docs/faq). Automations persist "across sessions and restarts until you turn it off" and each run "starts a fresh agent conversation with no memory of previous runs" (/docs/commands/automation). An always-on local instance is `agy remote-control start`, which "stays connected whenever your machine is powered on" (/docs/remote-control).
- **What the user supplies or builds for sustained work.** A Google account and plan (or a Gemini API key for the SDK: `export GEMINI_API_KEY`). Projects and their folders, or remote resources (GitHub repositories, Drive files, uploads). Any standing agent: custom agents are Markdown files the user writes ("You can define reusable custom subagents in Markdown format (.md) with YAML frontmatter"). Anything the agent should remember, written as rules or skills ("unless it’s written down as a customization"). For each unattended job, a self-contained prompt and scoped grants, because "Unattended runs automatically deny anything that would normally ask for your approval". Event-driven starts, a record of which agent or area owns which responsibility, per-agent identities, a secret store for local credentials, version rollback and evaluation across runs are not supplied and would have to be built on hooks, sidecars, plugins or the SDK.

# Disclosures and what could not be opened

- No file under `` was opened other than `prior-work/vendors/protocol-v2.md` and `prior-work/rerate-criteria-v2.md`. A directory listing of `prior-work/vendors/` showed the names `claude-code.md`, `codex.md`, `protocol.md` and `reader-brief.md`; none was opened.
- WebFetch returned only redirect stubs for `antigravity.google/docs` and `/changelog`, so pages were fetched with curl and converted to text locally. Images, videos and interactive demos on the pages were not viewed, so anything shown only in a screenshot is not reflected here.
- `agy models` contacted the vendor's service to list models for the signed-in account. No agent session was started, no prompt was sent and no configuration was changed.
- The managed "Antigravity agent" on the Gemini API (ai.google.dev) uses "the same harness as the Antigravity IDE" and is in preview. It was treated as a separate product from the App, CLI and SDK and no value rests on it. If it were counted, Scheduling (cron "Triggers" as a persistent resource) and Environments would gain evidence, and the "Where it runs" answer would add a vendor-hosted API.
- Not opened: the Antigravity App itself (not installed here) and the web app at antigravity.google.com (needs sign-in); the request-response logging page on docs.cloud.google.com (downloaded, not read); the SDK repository's component READMEs and example code; the "Environments" and "Building Custom Agents" pages on ai.google.dev; the Marketplace catalog inside the product (plugin names come from the launch post).
- `/docs/knowledge`, `/docs/knowledge-items`, `/docs/memory` and `/docs/memories` return 404; the IDE agent page lists "Knowledge" as a core component with no linked page.
- Two pages disagree on Remote Agents availability: `/docs/remote-agents` says "is rolling out gradually", and the changelog for App v2.30.0 (2026-11-09) says "Voice mode and remote agents have also finished rolling out."
- Availability labels differ by account type: several features (Auto preset, Remote Agents, Knowledge Work layout, built-in browser automation, Orchestrator) are stated as not available on business or enterprise accounts.
